name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (battle/animation domain). Descriptor accurately reflects behaviour: animate the turn-phase banner sliding out with a palette fade-out. No Ghidra address residue in the name. Confirmed by caller fd2_run_full_turn_cycle which invokes it as the slide-out half paired with fd2_animate_phase_banner_slide_in (Phase D enemy 0x52, Phase F player 0x50).
purpose: Plays the turn-phase banner ("ENEMY TURN" / "PLAYER TURN") slide-out animation: palette fade-out over the banner, then restores the battle scene and slides the two banner halves out to the screen edges.
logic_summary: Allocates a 64000-byte scratch frame and clears it to black. Phase 1 (17-frame palette fade-out, fade_iter 0x10..0 counting down, scroll_offset 0x11 counting down): each frame scrolls the source block into the scratch frame, blits the main banner sprite (banner_sprite_id) at (0x59,0x56) and the corner-frame sprite 0x51 at (0xA9,0x56) -- each blit returns its own freshly malloc'd save buffer that is freed immediately after -- fades the VGA palette down (brightness 16..0), pushes the frame to VGA 0xA0000, and waits 1 BIOS tick. The scratch frame is freed once after the loop. Phase 2 restores the battle scene: recomposite the battle tile map (stride 456) and overlay all chars. Phase 3 (5-frame slide-out, x_offset = iter*0x19 = 0,0x19,0x32,0x4B,0x64) calls fd2_render_phase_banner_frame to slide the banner halves out to the edges.

params.name: banner_sprite_id
params.semantics: Sprite index of the turn-phase banner to animate (caller passes 0x52 = ENEMY TURN, 0x50 = PLAYER TURN). Used as the sprite-index argument to the per-frame fd2_alloc_and_blit_indexed_sprite_chunk blit in the fade loop and to fd2_render_phase_banner_frame in the slide-out loop.
params.reason: Name accurately describes the value (a banner sprite ID) and matches both caller usage and body usage. No address residue, not a param_N placeholder.

returns.semantics: No return value; side effects are the on-screen animation and restoration of the battle scene into the working buffer.

notes: Source comment block (anicombt.c lines 1185-1215) is already precise, ASCII, and correct, including a NOTE documenting the Ghidra EAX-tracking artifact (collapsed blit/memmove return temporaries and hoisted frees) -- the encoded C matches the assembly (each blit's save buffer freed right after; scratch freed once after the loop). No equivalence/logic bug: the EAX artifact is a documented decompiler quirk, not a code defect. Ghidra plate (Traditional Chinese, allowed for plates) is consistent with the refined understanding; left unchanged. No source edit needed (comment kept). Caller fd2_run_full_turn_cycle confirms the slide-in/slide-out pairing and the 0x50/0x52 banner sprite IDs.
